newsitem.title: USA: StatsCan report seen slightly bullish for canola.
newsitem.headline: StatsCan report seen slightly bullish for canola.

text.p: News that Statistics Canada had cut its Canadian canola production estimate by around 350,000 tonnes was seen as slightly bullish for canola futures with the final total expected to be even lower, analysts said.
"I think the final numbers will be smaller yet so I think it is definitely a bullish canola number," Linnco Futures Group analyst Rob Dzisiak said.
Statistics Canada estimated Canadian canola production at 4.979 million tonnes, down from a previous projection, issued in late August, of 5.337 million.
Analysts said the impact of the market may be limited as a downward revision had been anticipated.

"The trade was looking for a smaller number but this is towards the low end of expectations. We go from an adequate carryout to an extremely tight carryout and a point where we have got to ration demand," LFG's Dzisiak said.
He estimated canola futures on the Winnipeg Commodity Exchange may open about C$2.00 higher based on the data.
"In the summer things looked fantastic and I think the yields have been quite disappointing," Dzisiak said.
United Grain Growers analyst Mike Jubinville also expected the final production total to be lower.
The latest Statistics Canada report was based on conditions as of September 16 and problems have got worse since then, Jubinville noted.

"Since we got into September conditions have deteriorated and we had some fairly extensive harvest delays. Canola yields are looking very good in Manitoba but when we go further west things begin to deteriorate quickly, especially in Alberta," UGG's Jubinville said.
Dzisiak said most other StatsCan estimates were broadly in line with expectations, although the Canadian barley total at 15.992 million tonnes was slightly smaller than anticipated.
The barley total included a projection for western Canada of 15.095 million tonnes. Earlier this month UGG projected a barley crop in western Canada of 15.56 million tonnes.
"The discrepancy between our numbers and StatsCan has to do with differences in production in Alberta and that one is a toss up at this point in time," UGG's Jubinville said.

"Nevertheless it is going to be an all time record for a barley crop in western Canada so I am certainly not looking for any sustained rally developing in barley market based on these kind of numbers," he added.
